newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's Frei shakes up Cabinet.
newsitem.headline: Chile's Frei shakes up Cabinet.

text.p: Chilean President Eduardo Frei replaced his top adviser, Chief-of-Staff Genaro Arriagada, and four other Cabinet ministers on Friday in a shakeup only a month before nationwide municipal elections.

Frei had asked for the resignations of his entire cabinet and accepted those of Arriagada and the ministers of education, agriculture, planning and transport and communications, said presidential spokesman Jose Joaquin Brunner.

Local media had expected a reshuffle this week, partly to give a fresher image to Frei's center-left coalition government before nationwide municipal elections on October 27. The elections are seen as an important political test for Frei, who took office for a six-year term in 1994.
Arriagada will be replaced by Juan Villarzu, the president of state copper company Codelco and a leader of Frei's Christian Democratic party.
There was no official word on Arriagada's future but officials have said privately he was tipped to be the next ambassador to the United States.

Arriagada, Frei's top political adviser, had taken criticism for a series of missteps since Frei took office, including the defeat in Congress of constitutional reforms aimed at curbing the military's power. His removal had long been expected.

The most surprising change was in education, in which Sergio Molina was replaced by Budget Chief Jose Pablo Arellano, who only an hour before the reshuffle had held a news conference to announce the government's 1997 budget.

Arellano is a well-known economist. Like all the new appointees, he is considerably younger than the person he is replacing, reinforcing reports in local media that Frei sought a younger image for his government.

Agriculture Minister Emiliano Ortega was replaced by chief trade negotiator Carlos Mladinic and Transport and Communications Minister Narciso Irureta was replaced by his number two, Transport Secretary Claudio Hohmann.
Planning Minister Luis Maira was replaced by economist Roberto Pizarro.

Mladinic was best known as chief negotiator of Chile's recent free trade agreement with the four-nation Mercosur bloc. His appointment as agriculture minister is likely to be seen as a blow to farmers who angrily opposed the Mercosur pact, charging it will flood Chile with cheap Argentine grain.
The Cabinet reshuffle was the second in Frei's 30 month old government, after a shakeup of key political ministers in late 1994.

Local news media have said Frei wanted to present a fresher face before the October 27 elections, in which candidates from the four parties in the Concertacion coalition face tough challenges from rightist candidates.
The elections are Chile's last major political test before congressional elections in 1997 and then presidential polls in 1999, in which Frei is barred from seeking re-election.
